summary: Tenant activation wave causing ephemeral GPU depletion and autoscaler lag
description:
Issue summary: HelixCare reported intermittent 429s and p99 latency spikes on dedicated cluster during a morning activation window. Impact: Several routes backed by the customer's reserved pool experienced elevated token latency and transient request failures for ~40 minutes. Customer-facing symptoms included streaming disconnects and repeated retry errors.

Observed behavior: p50 latency normal, p95/p99 spiked; autoscaler did not provision additional nodes quickly enough; allocator showed many short-lived attachments from the customer's sidecars; GPU attach failures and slot exhaustion recorded in the allocator and scheduler logs.

Initial customer report: customer saw a synchronous activation burst from a scheduled job that bootstraps short lived model shims across many pods, creating ~10-15k ephemeral connections over 2 minutes. This coincided with spike in sidecar write amplification and NVMe IO wait on the dedicated hosts.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support): collected request traces and error counts, confirmed 429s across multiple routes. Observed repeated 'slot-reserved' and 'attach-timeout' in allocator logs.

SRE analysis: correlated allocator metrics with NVMe iostat and kernel iowait. Found marked increase in sidecar log writes and metadata updates at 09:05 UTC, matching customer's activation window. Autoscaler metrics show scale decision delayed by 45s due to noisy telemetry from a background health-sweep (high IO causing heartbeat jitter).

Key log snippets: 
2026-03-10T09:05:12Z scheduler INFO attaching slot tenant=helixcare slot_id=shard-117 status=queued
2026-03-10T09:05:28Z allocator WARN attach-timeout tenant=helixcare reason=nvme_iowait_high
2026-03-10T09:06:10Z autoscaler DEBUG decision=hold reason=telemetry-latency(1200ms)

Hypotheses considered: sidecar log flood triggering host IO saturation -> allocator heartbeat delays -> autoscaler misread (thinks nodes not under pressure) -> delayed provisioning -> ephemeral connection fanout causes slot fragmentation. Also considered network spike and model prefetch churn; NVMe IO correlated best with symptoms.

2026-03-10 09:07 UTC: Support opened incident, gathered traces.
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: SRE observed NVMe iowait spike and allocator attach-timeouts.
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (throttle sidecar write rate for helixcare).
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Autoscaler headroom increased for affected reserved pool (manual bump).
2026-03-10 09:42 UTC: Error rate subsided and latency returned to baseline.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Follow-up completed, permanent fixes scheduled.
resolution:
Short-term mitigation: applied customer-scoped sidecar write throttling and small default rate-limit to prevent NVMe write amplification during activation waves. Manually increased reserved-pool headroom (added +2 nodes) while autoscaler logic was adjusted.

Long-term fixes scheduled: 1) autoscaler change to ignore short telemetry bursts from background health scans and require sustained pressure before deferring scale decisions (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/98). 2) allocator patch to aggregate rapid attach/detach from same tenant to reduce slot churn (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/204). 3) documentation & template for customers with large activation waves recommending staggered start or baked-in rate-limiting.

Customer communication: Support coordinated with HelixCare engineering; provided workaround to stagger activation and confirmation when root cause mitigations were scheduled. Issue marked Resolved after validation period of 48 hours with no recurrence.
